elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Amended 13.4 reads "each party's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed payments made to M&I by Customer ... during the twelve (12) months prior to the event", replacing the one-sided "M&I's total liability".

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The rendered cap is only "payments made to M&I by Customer ... during the twelve (12) months prior to the event" — no USD 1,000,000 floor and "payments made" is paid-only, not "paid or payable".

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 13.2: "Neither Customer nor M&I shall be liable for ... any indirect, incidental, punitive, special or consequential damages ...".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "Except for indemnification obligations, breach of confidentiality obligations, gross negligence and willful misconduct, which are uncapped ...".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out list contains no data protection or security obligations; only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct are excepted.
"Except for indemnification obligations ... which are uncapped" in amended 13.4, placing Section 14.2 indemnities outside the cap.
Gross negligence is named in the uncapped exception list in amended 13.4.
"willful misconduct" is named in the uncapped exception list in amended 13.4.
Fraud is absent from the carve-out list in the rendered 13.4.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: No language states that Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes; the retained proviso only exempts collection actions from the one-year limitation period, not from the cap.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "each party's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed ..." — cap now runs to both Customer and M&I.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Basis changed from three (3) months to "payments made to M&I by Customer under this Agreement during the twelve (12) months prior to the event".
Express "Except for indemnification obligations ... which are uncapped" opener to 13.4.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "breach of confidentiality obligations" listed among uncapped exceptions.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the single capping sentence in 13.4 now applies to "each party", uses a twelve-month payments basis, and expressly places indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct outside the cap.

Preferred level is incomplete (no USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor, "payments made" rather than fees paid or payable, and no data protection/security, fraud, IP-infringement or Customer-payment-obligation carve-outs) — acceptable because the claim targets the fallback.

Minimal: only the operative capping clause was edited. The mutual consequential-damages exclusion in 13.2 and the one-year suit limitation with its collection proviso in 13.4 are retained verbatim; no survival tails, expense language, procedures or extra carve-outs were added.

The replaced "Notwithstanding any provision in this Agreement" lead-in is a necessary casualty of inserting the "Except for ... which are uncapped" opener; retaining a blanket override alongside the new super-cap exceptions would create a contradictory retained phrase, and its removal is Customer-neutral-to-favourable.

Preserves intent: the limitation period, collection carve-out, Section 14.2 indemnities and Section 13.2 exclusions all survive without contradiction; no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is introduced.
Original clause correctly classified as a deviation — it hit two walk-away triggers (Vendor-only cap; cap below six months' fees) and left indemnities inside the cap.

If pressing for the preferred position later, the drafter should add the greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor, change "payments made to M&I" to "fees paid or payable", extend the carve-out list to data protection/security, fraud and infringement of the other party's IP, and add an express statement that Customer's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap.
